mainTopic: זימון limits, wine with and without water, respect for bread and food, and forgetting a ברכה with food in one's mouth
overview: The amud opens by finishing the case of three people from three groups who want to form a זימון together. רבא limits it: this only works if their original groups never counted them in a זימון. He proves it from a משנה about a split bed, whose lost טומאה does not come back when it is repaired. The גמרא then teaches that a shared שמש joins two groups into one. Next comes the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and חכמים about wine without water: does it get בורא פרי הגפן, and may it be used to wash hands? Even חכמים agree that a כוס של ברכה needs water, because of מצוה מן המובחר. A ברייתא then lists four ways to respect bread. A story with מר זוטרא and רב אשי leads to the rule that other foods may be thrown only if they will not get ruined, which also explains the wedding custom of throwing nuts. The amud ends with what to do if someone put food in his mouth before saying the ברכה: swallow a drink, spit out food that stays clean, and move aside food that would become disgusting.

steps.title: The three can only join if their old groups did not already count them
steps.stepSummary: The case of three people from three groups forming a new זימון is limited. It only applies if their original groups never included them in a זימון. If they were already included, their זימון obligation is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when those original groups did not first include them in a זימון in their own place. But if they did include them in a זימון in their own place, the זימון obligation has 'flown away' from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule that three people from three different groups can form a זימון together. It only works if their old groups never counted them in a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these three people is obligated in זימון only because of the group he first ate with. If that group already said זימון and counted him, he has already fulfilled that obligation. Nothing is left for him to bring into a new group.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this rule in the case of...
They included them in the זימון
The זימון obligation has 'flown away' from them, meaning it is gone

steps.confusionAlert: 'פרח' does not mean the people lost something by mistake. It means their obligation was already used up, because they were counted in the first group's זימון.

phrases.english: And we only said this
phrases.notes: Introduces a limit on the previous rule

phrases.english: where those people did not first
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the members of the original groups

phrases.english: include them in a zimmun in their own place,
but if they did include them in a zimmun in their own place —
the zimmun obligation has 'flown away' from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the earlier rule (on the previous amud) about three people from three groups forming a זימון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people from three groups can join for a זימון only if their original groups did not already count them in a זימון.

steps.title: רבא brings a source about a split bed
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where he learns this idea from. He quotes a משנה: a bed that was half stolen, half lost, or divided between brothers or partners becomes טהור. If the pieces are put back together, it can become impure only from now on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say this? As we learned in a משנה: a bed that half of it was stolen, or half of it was lost, or brothers or partners divided it, is pure. If they put it back together, it can receive impurity from now on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets up a proof for the rule in step 1. He quotes a משנה about an impure bed that was broken apart and later put back together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken utensil is no longer a real כלי, so the טומאה it had goes away. Once it is fixed, it is a כלי again and can become impure in the future. The key words are 'from now on', and רבא will build his proof on them in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I derive this?
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this? —
As we learned: A bed, half of which was stolen,
phrases.notes: The bed was impure before this happened

phrases.english: or half of which was lost,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁחֲלָקוּהָ אַחִין אוֹ שׁוּתָּפִין — טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: or brothers or partners divided it — it is pure.
phrases.notes: A broken utensil is no longer a utensil, so its impurity leaves

phrases.english: If they put it back together — it can receive impurity from now on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the rule in step 1
steps.raayaObject: The rule that once people were counted in a זימון, their obligation is gone for good
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a bed that was split and then put back together

steps.title: What is gone does not come back
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the משנה closely. The bed becomes impure 'from now on', but the old טומאה does not come back. So once the bed was split, its טומאה left forever. In the same way, once someone was counted in a זימון, the obligation left forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From now on', yes. Backwards, no. We see that once they divided it, the impurity left it. Here too, once they included them in the זימון, the זימון obligation left them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws an inference from the words of the משנה and applies it to זימון. This finishes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From now on' tells us the old impurity does not come back when the bed is fixed. Splitting it removed the impurity permanently. In the same way, being counted in a זימון removed the obligation permanently, even after the person leaves to join others.

keyTerms.meaning: Backwards in time, applying to the past
It is clear from this; apparently
Here too, in the same way

steps.whatToRemember: An obligation or status that has already 'flown away' does not come back. A split bed does not get its old טומאה back, and someone already counted in a זימון does not get his זימון obligation back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: three people from three groups can make a new זימון only if no one counted them before they left.

phrases.english: From now on — yes,
backwards — no.
So we see: once they divided it —
the impurity 'flew away' from it.
Here too, once they included them in the zimmun,
the zimmun obligation 'flew away' from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 2 and applies it to זימון
steps.raayaObject: Once someone was counted in a זימון, the obligation does not come back
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'from now on' in the משנה about the bed show that the old טומאה does not return

steps.title: A shared waiter joins two groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about two groups eating in one house. A ברייתא teaches that if one שמש serves both groups, he joins them into one group for זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Two groups', etc. It was taught in a ברייתא: If there is a waiter between them, the waiter joins them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about two groups in one house. It then adds a ברייתא: a שמש who serves both groups connects them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said two groups join together if some of them can see each other. The ברייתא adds another way they can join: one waiter going back and forth between them makes them count as one group, even if they cannot see each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote of the משנה continues
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: 'Two groups', etc.
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה to start a new topic

phrases.english: It was taught: If there is a waiter between them —
the waiter joins them together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared שמש who serves two groups joins them into one group for זימון.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: wine without water is not yet real wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'אין מברכין על היין' and brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי אליעזר rules that wine without water gets בורא פרי העץ and may be used to wash hands. Once water is added, it gets בורא פרי הגפן and may not be used for washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'We do not say a blessing over wine.' The Rabbis taught: before water is put into wine, we do not say 'בורא פרי הגפן' over it, only 'בורא פרי העץ', and you may wash your hands with it. Once water is put in, we say 'בורא פרי הגפן' over it and you may not wash your hands with it. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that spells out רבי אליעזר's opinion about wine without water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, adding water is what turns the liquid into proper drinkable wine. Before that, it counts like plain fruit juice: it gets the general fruit ברכה, and it is not 'important' enough to forbid using it for washing. After water is added, it becomes real wine, with its own special ברכה and its own respect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
The special ברכה for wine: 'Who creates the fruit of the vine.'
The general ברכה for fruit of a tree.
Washing one's hands (נטילת ידים) with it.
'These are the words of רבי אליעזר.' This marks whose opinion it is.

steps.confusionAlert: Wine in the times of the גמרא was very strong and thick. People normally diluted it with water before drinking. So 'wine without water' does not mean ordinary wine as we know it. It means a concentrate that was hardly drinkable.

phrases.english: One does not recite a blessing over the wine.
phrases.notes: Quoting the words of the משנה (רבי אליעזר's view).

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם —
phrases.english: Wine, before one has put water into it —
one does not recite over it 'Who creates fruit of the vine'
but rather 'Who creates fruit of the tree.'
And one may wash hands with it.
Once he has put water into it —
one recites over it 'Who creates fruit of the vine,'
and one may not wash hands with it,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the שמש topic to the next line of the משנה, about wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, undiluted wine gets בורא פרי העץ and may be used for washing hands. Diluted wine gets בורא פרי הגפן and may not.

steps.title: חכמים: it is wine either way
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר. Whether or not water was added, the ברכה is בורא פרי הגפן, and you may not wash your hands with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: either way, we say 'בורא פרי הגפן' over it, and we do not wash hands with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving the opposing view of חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, wine is wine even before water is added. So it always gets its special ברכה, and it is always too important to use for washing. Both of רבי אליעזר's rules for undiluted wine are rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the Sages say.' This introduces the majority opinion.
'Either way.' Here: whether or not water was added.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
in either case,
one recites over it 'Who creates fruit of the vine'
and one may not wash hands with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine gets בורא פרי הגפן and may not be used for washing hands, whether diluted or not.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: without water it is not yet real wine (בורא פרי העץ, may wash with it). חכמים: it is wine either way (בורא פרי הגפן, may not wash with it).

steps.title: Whose view matches שמואל's rule about bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side of the מחלוקת fits שמואל's rule that a person may use bread for all his needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this follow, what שמואל said: 'A person may do all his needs with bread'? Whose opinion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא in the ברייתא fits שמואל's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allows using bread for purposes other than eating, and does not see this as disrespecting food. The ברייתא also argues about using a food (wine) for a non-food purpose (washing hands). So the גמרא wants to know which side שמואל matches.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view does it follow?' A question asking which side a rule matches.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which Shmuel said:
a person may perform all his needs with bread,
in accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links an outside rule (שמואל) to the מחלוקת just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא in the ברייתא שמואל's rule about using bread for non-food needs agrees with.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שמואל follows רבי אליעזר, who allows undiluted wine to be used for washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: שמואל's rule fits רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר lets a person wash his hands with undiluted wine, which means using food for a non-eating purpose. That is the same idea as שמואל's rule for bread. חכמים forbid washing with wine, so they would not fit שמואל as well.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's rule matches רבי אליעזר, who permits using undiluted wine for washing hands.

steps.title: חכמים agree about the כוס של ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר in one case: on a כוס של ברכה, the ברכה is not said until water is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: the Sages agree with רבי אליעזר regarding a cup of blessing, that we do not say the ברכה over it until water is put in.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a limit to the מחלוקת. In one special case, the cup used for a ברכה like ברכת המזון, even חכמים require water first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים normally say undiluted wine is real wine. Still, for a כוס של ברכה they agree it should be diluted first. This is an exception for a מצוה cup. It does not change חכמים's basic view that undiluted wine counts as wine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They agree.' Used when one side concedes a point to the other.
The cup of wine over which a ברכה such as ברכת המזון is said.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina said:
the Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer
regarding a cup of blessing
that one does not recite the blessing over it
until he puts water into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת by showing a case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a כוס של ברכה, everyone agrees water must be added before the ברכה is said.

steps.title: Why do חכמים agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason חכמים agree in the case of a כוס של ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why חכמים change their view for this cup. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חכמים hold that undiluted wine is real wine, it seems it should be good enough for a כוס של ברכה too. So the גמרא wants the reason for the exception.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why חכמים require water for a כוס של ברכה when they normally treat undiluted wine as wine.

steps.title: A מצוה should be done in the best way
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא explains: a מצוה should be done in the finest way possible, and diluted wine is the better drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: we need the מצוה to be done in the choicest way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא gives the reason: מצוה מן המובחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים still hold that undiluted wine is technically wine. But a מצוה deserves the best, and properly diluted wine is the best way to drink it. So for a כוס של ברכה they require water.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing a מצוה in the choicest, finest way.

steps.whyThisMatters: מצוה מן המובחר is a general principle. It explains many halachos where something technically valid is still upgraded for a מצוה.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
We require a מצוה to be done in the choicest manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: בָּעֵינַן מִצְוָה מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצוה should be done in the best manner, and diluted wine is the best.

steps.title: What is undiluted wine good for, according to חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if חכמים treat undiluted wine as real wine, what is it actually useful for, since it is too strong to drink?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the Rabbis, what is it fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about חכמים's view. This sets up רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Undiluted wine was too strong to drink normally. If it is barely usable, why do חכמים give it the full status of wine? The גמרא wants to know what real use it has.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what is it fit?' What use does it have?

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, for what is it fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to חכמים's view from step 6 and asks how it makes sense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical use undiluted wine has, which would justify חכמים treating it as full wine.

steps.title: It is good for a medicinal drink
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that undiluted wine is useful for קורייטי, a medicinal drink made of wine and oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: it is fit for קורייטי (a medicinal wine-and-oil drink).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the answer: undiluted wine has a real use, as a remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since undiluted wine has a real, valuable use, it is an important drink. That supports חכמים's view that it is real wine, with בורא פרי הגפן and no washing hands with it.

keyTerms.meaning: A medicinal drink made of wine and oil.

steps.whatToRemember: חכמים: undiluted wine is real wine, because it has a real use (קורייטי). Even so, for a כוס של ברכה they require water, because of מצוה מן המובחר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is fit for koraiytei (a medicinal drink).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Undiluted wine is used for קורייטי, a medicinal drink, so it has real value as wine.

steps.title: Four rules of respect for bread
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four things one may not do to bread, all meant to keep bread from being ruined or treated with disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Four things were said about bread. Do not put raw meat on bread. Do not pass a full cup over bread. Do not throw bread. Do not use bread to prop up a dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with four rules about treating bread with respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rules protect bread from being ruined: raw meat may drip blood on it, and a full cup may spill on it. The other two protect its dignity: throwing it, or using it as a tool to hold up a plate, treats it as worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין זורקין את הפת' is the starting point for the whole discussion that follows about throwing other foods.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Four things were said about bread:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַנִּיחִין בָּשָׂר חַי עַל הַפַּת.
phrases.english: One may not place raw meat on bread.
phrases.notes: Its blood could drip onto the bread and spoil it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַעֲבִירִין כּוֹס מָלֵא עַל הַפַּת.
phrases.english: And one may not pass a full cup over bread.
phrases.notes: It could spill and ruin the bread.

phrases.english: And one may not throw bread.
And one may not prop up a dish with bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּפַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: moves from the discussion of wine to rules of respect for bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread must not be put where it can be spoiled, thrown, or used as a prop under a dish.

steps.title: מר זוטרא throws fruit to רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: A story: while eating with אמימר and רב אשי, מר זוטרא throws a portion of fruit to רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר, מר זוטרא and רב אשי were eating bread together. Dates and pomegranates were brought to them. מר זוטרא took some and threw a portion in front of רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next move: an action that looks like it breaks the rule of not throwing food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא throws fruit, not bread. This sets up the question of whether the ban on throwing applies only to bread or to all foods.

phrases.english: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi
were eating bread together,
dates and pomegranates were brought before them.
Mar Zutra took (some)
and threw a portion in front of Rav Ashi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי כְּרַכוּ רִיפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case that tests how far the bread rule from the ברייתא reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר זוטרא threw fruit, which looks like it may conflict with the ban on throwing food.

steps.title: רב אשי objects: one may not throw food
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges מר זוטרא with a ברייתא that says one may not throw food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Doesn't the Master agree with what was taught, 'One may not throw food'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks מר זוטרא how he could throw the fruit, quoting a ברייתא that bans throwing food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is worded as a question, but it is really a challenge. רב אשי reads the ברייתא as covering all foods, so throwing fruit looks forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the Master hold this view?
That which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him:
Does the Master not hold
with that which was taught:
'One may not throw food'?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר זוטרא's action in the story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids throwing food, and fruit is food, so the throw should be forbidden.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: that rule is about bread
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the ברייתא forbidding throwing was said only about bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling was taught about bread.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends himself: the ban on throwing is only about bread, not about fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He narrows the rule. The ברייתא that bans throwing (like the one in step 14) is about bread, so other foods like fruit may be thrown.

phrases.english: That was taught about bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on throwing covers all foods.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on throwing applies only to bread.

steps.title: רב אשי: a ברייתא says the same as bread
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings another ברייתא that explicitly puts other foods in the same category as bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: Just as one may not throw bread, so too one may not throw other foods!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back with a ברייתא that clearly compares all foods to bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא blocks מר זוטרא's answer. It names bread and then says other foods follow the same rule, so the ban cannot be limited to bread.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught? (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
Just as one may not throw bread,
so too one may not throw other foods!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין זוֹרְקִין אֶת הַפַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects מר זוטרא's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that the ban is only on bread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly extends the throwing ban from bread to all foods.

steps.title: מר זוטרא brings an opposite ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers with a different ברייתא that says other foods may be thrown, unlike bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said to him: But wasn't it taught: Even though one may not throw bread, one may throw other foods!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא supports his position with a ברייתא that says the exact opposite of רב אשי's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other: one bans throwing all foods, and one allows throwing foods other than bread. This sets up the need for a solution.
steps.confusionAlert: Both rabbis use the same word 'וְהָתַנְיָא', but they quote opposite ברייתות. Track who is speaking: step 18 is רב אשי, and this step is מר זוטרא.

phrases.english: He (Mar Zutra) said to him: But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זוֹרְקִין אֶת הַפַּת,
phrases.english: Even though one may not throw bread,
one may throw other foods!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָתַנְיָא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זוֹרְקִין אֶת הַפַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's ברייתא with a conflicting ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: מר זוטרא's view that foods other than bread may be thrown
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'אף על פי שאין זורקין את הפת, אבל זורקין את האוכלין'

steps.title: Resolving the two ברייתות: does the food get ruined?
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות do not argue: food that gets ruined when thrown may not be thrown, and food that stays clean may be thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difficulty. This ברייתא is about food that gets disgusting when thrown, and that ברייתא is about food that does not get disgusting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by showing that each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on throwing other foods applies to soft foods that get squashed or dirty. Hard foods, like the dates and pomegranates in the story, are not ruined, so throwing them is allowed, and מר זוטרא was right.
steps.whatToRemember: Bread may never be thrown. Other foods may be thrown only if they do not get ruined or dirty by it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical rule for throwing food, and it is the background for the wedding ברייתא that follows.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is about an item that becomes disgusting (when thrown),
that one is about an item that does not become disgusting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the ברייתות in steps 18 and 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different kinds of food)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly argue about whether other foods may be thrown.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food that gets ruined may not be thrown, and food that stays clean may be thrown.

steps.title: Wine and food before a חתן and כלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: wine may be poured through pipes before a חתן and כלה, and roasted grain and nuts may be thrown in summer but not in the rainy season, while cakes may never be thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may run wine through pipes before a חתן and כלה. One may throw roasted grain and nuts before them in the summer, but not in the rainy season. But one may not throw cakes, not in the summer and not in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about wedding customs that shows the rule of throwing food in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In summer, thrown grain and nuts land on dry ground and can still be eaten, so they are not ruined. In the rainy season they land in mud and get ruined, so it is forbidden. גלוסקאות are a kind of bread, and bread may never be thrown (step 14), so they are forbidden in every season.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether throwing food is allowed depends on whether the food will be ruined. The same nuts can be allowed in summer and forbidden in the rainy season.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may run wine through pipes
before a groom and before a bride,
phrases.notes: As a sign of blessing and plenty.

phrases.english: and one may throw roasted grain and nuts before them
in the summer,
but not in the rainy season.
phrases.notes: They would fall into mud and be ruined.

phrases.english: But not cakes,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלָא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: neither in the summer nor in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַמְשִׁיכִין יַיִן בְּצִנּוֹרוֹת לִפְנֵי חָתָן וְלִפְנֵי כַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא that follows the same principle as step 20: throwing is allowed only when the food is not ruined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain and nuts may be thrown before a חתן and כלה in summer but not in the rainy season, and cakes may never be thrown.

steps.title: Forgot the blessing with food already in his mouth
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that someone who put food in his mouth without a ברכה should move it to one side of his mouth and then make the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If a person forgot and put food into his mouth without making a ברכה, he should push the food to one side of his mouth and then make the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רב יהודה about a person who forgot to make a ברכה before eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person cannot simply swallow, because then he would be eating without a ברכה. He also cannot make a ברכה with food blocking his mouth. רב יהודה's solution is to push the food to the side so his mouth is free enough to speak the ברכה properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A blessing (here, the blessing before eating)
He moves them aside (to one side of the mouth)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה that comes up often. It is the starting point for the three ברייתות that follow.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If one forgot and put food
into his mouth without a blessing —
he moves them to one side and recites the blessing.
phrases.notes: He pushes the food to one side of his mouth, so he can say the ברכה clearly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It is no longer about throwing food before a חתן and כלה; now it is about forgetting a ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If food is already in the mouth without a ברכה, move it to one side and make the ברכה.

steps.title: Three teachings give three different instructions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes three ברייתות that seem to contradict each other: one says to swallow the food, one says to spit it out, and one says to move it aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: he swallows the food. Another ברייתא teaches: he spits it out. A third ברייתא teaches: he moves it aside in his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that three ברייתות seem to argue about what to do with the food in this case. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will resolve the conflict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No question word appears here, but quoting three opposite answers side by side works as a challenge: which one is right? The third ברייתא matches רב יהודה. The other two seem to disagree with him and with each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in one ברייתא
It was taught in another ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Swallowing is not a general license to skip the ברכה. The next step limits it to drinks: a drink cannot be held to the side of the mouth, and spitting it out would waste it, so for drinks alone the ברייתא lets him swallow that mouthful.

phrases.english: It was taught in one baraita: He swallows them,
and it was taught in another: He spits them out,
and it was taught in another: He moves them aside.
phrases.notes: This third ברייתא matches רב יהודה's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא חֲדָא בּוֹלְעָן וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ פּוֹלְטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings sources on רב יהודה's case that seem to contradict each other and two of which seem to contradict him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the ברייתות, and רב יהודה's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three sources give three opposite instructions for the same situation, so they appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: Each teaching is about a different kind of food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: swallowing applies to drinks, spitting out applies to food that does not become disgusting, and moving aside applies to food that would become disgusting.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a contradiction. The ברייתא that says 'he swallows' is talking about drinks. The one that says 'he spits out' is talking about food that does not become disgusting when taken out of the mouth. The one that says 'he moves it aside' is talking about food that does become disgusting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different type of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A drink cannot be held to the side or spat out and reused, so he swallows it. A food that stays edible can be spat out, and after the ברכה he can eat it again, so nothing is lost. A food that would become disgusting if spat out should not be wasted, so he only moves it aside, as רב יהודה said.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no real contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: Drinks: swallow. Food that stays clean: spit out, make the ברכה, then eat. Food that would become disgusting: move it to the side of the mouth and make the ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This follows the same idea as the earlier discussion about throwing food: we try not to ruin or waste food. Food that would become disgusting is treated differently from food that stays clean.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This one that taught 'he swallows them' is about liquids.
And this one that taught 'he spits them out'
is about an item that does not become disgusting.
phrases.notes: He can spit it out, make the ברכה, and eat it afterward.

phrases.english: And this one that taught 'he moves them aside'
is about an item that becomes disgusting.
phrases.notes: Spitting it out would ruin it, so he only moves it to the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא בּוֹלְעָן בְּמַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 23 by dividing the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: each ברייתא is about a different type of food
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three ברייתות disagree about the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא deals with a different type of food (drink, food that stays clean, food that becomes disgusting), so they all agree, and רב יהודה's ruling fits the food that becomes disgusting.
